Here's a visual guide for enabling Memory for your ChatGPT account. This might get patched (they change their A/B system) if many people use it but it's working as of 2024-03-20.

No technical understanding is required, but you need to be able to follow instructions.

1. Go to https://t.co/Xshojpeprb and log into your account

(This should work regardless of if you're paying for ChatGPT Plus or not.) https://t.co/G4YcPYSdeP

2. Open your browser's DevTools. For Chromium-based browsers like Chrome, you can right-click on the page and press Inspect

(Ctrl+Shift+i won't work because OpenAI overrides it to open Custom Instructions) https://t.co/hEs7Sgx7Yo
3. Press on the Network tab inside DevTools. You can see the different tabs at the top. You'll be shown a screen like this https://t.co/FZ8ZBivkvp

4. Press Ctrl+r to refresh the page. Don't close DevTools.

You should see that the Network tab is now populated with many different entries (HTTP requests the page makes) https://t.co/hWnhvFenCm
5. Find the "v4-2023-04-27" request. You can locate it by typing e.g. "v4" into the Filter input in the top left https://t.co/cCxjiCHudc
6. Right click on the v4-2023-04-27 request and press "Override content" in the menu that pops up https://t.co/ZggoPEHobn
You will see a banner that asks you to select a folder. Use that to select one. https://t.co/oghV04DpM4
Then it will ask you to allow DevTools to access it. Press Allow https://t.co/Z7YduhCeMb

Once you've done that, DevTools will automatically switch to the Sources tab and show you the v4-2023-04-27 file. It should start with 
{"accounts":{"
and then your account ID, which will be different from mine. https://t.co/xaArOuFqV6
7. Press the "{ }" button in the bottom left to format the file https://t.co/hTiOgtIhLR

Once you format the file by pressing that button, it should look like this. If you format button doesn't work (it did nothing when pressed when I tried to replicate it on my friend's Mac), then you'll have to scroll through the file on one line https://t.co/qyFegImOxm
8. Find the "features" array inside the file and add (type to edit the file) a new entry called "sunshine_available". Once you're done, it should look like the second picture https://t.co/SXZcDDraFf

If you are doing it on one line, you'll have to scroll to the left until you see
"features": [
and then add it to the right of that

9. Inside the Sources window, press Ctrl+s to save the file.

If it's saved, you will see the filename say "v4-2023-04-27" with no star. If it's unsaved, it will say "v4-2023-04-27*" https://t.co/NngU5SzIyq

10. Refresh the page again

Now, you should see a popup like in https://t.co/WRXxgF4Byi showing that your account has access to Memory

Did you know? If two different Amazon listings include the same image as their thumbnail, it will be cached to only one image stored and served with the same URL across both. So I have to use the surrounding <a> to get the product ID to discern them

Overall workflow is
1. Impersonate browser TLS handshake to circumvent sniffing and retrieve HTML of search results
2. Search for "div.s-product-image-container a.a-link-normal"
3. Parse <a> href for ID, look at inner img.s-image src for thumbnail

Search engines don't seem to index every listing, but fortunately, the name parameter in
amazon co jp /name/dp/id
actually does nothing, so you can easily submit your id and have it show the correct item

1. have per-project memory stores of best practices and style conventions. have a few templates available that lets you easily specify to avoid using external packages when possible

4. have the LLM explicitly maintain quantitative or qualitative confidence in different points of understanding within changes, and require a far higher threshold than the current before declaring a request fulfilled

I think it seems doable, like
1. each parallel outputs their final best solution along with a key insight or summary of the technique
2. an agent filters the solutions list for duplicates 
3. you send every solution (likely not more than 10 or so fundamentally different ones) to every parallel agent besides the one they originally thought of
4. each parallel agent analyzes the new solutions and compares it to their original, providing a new best
5. you collect each new best solution and use a majority vote on them as the final agent group solution

step 4 works because in the usual case it's easier, for models and for humans, to compare answers and select the most correct one, vs produce the most correct one themselves. so as long as it's in the list, the overall best is likely chosen
